overview:

___________________________________________________________________________________________


University of California, Berkeley

UC Berkeley is the first campus of the University of California. It is the only campus authorized to use any of the names: University of California, Cal or Berkeley. Among the alumni, professors and researchers associated with the University, there are 65 Nobel Prize winners, 19 Oscars winners and 11 Pulitzer Prize winners.

The institution is ranked among the top 5 universities in the world alongside Harvard, Cambridge, Oxford, and Stanford. The University of Shanghai ranked it, in 2007 and 2008, in 3rd place among the best universities in the world.

Founded in 1891, UC Berkeley Extension is the continuing education branch of the prestigious University of California Berkeley. The school is spread over three campuses (Berkeley, San Francisco and Belmont) and offers students from around the world nearly 75 professional certificates and specialized programs. Its HAAS Business School is one of the best in the country.

Its diplomas and certificates are issued by professionals accredited by Berkeley and adhere to the quality and teaching standards defined by the university. At UC Berkeley Extension, you will be immersed in an active and diverse student community in the heart of San Francisco Bay, a region known for its entrepreneurial dynamism. Many of its programs are developed by experts in the field, who constantly adapt their lessons to the needs of the job market.The program at this university emphasizes entrepreneurship and innovation in digital and global markets.
administrative:
1. Application Dossier

You will work directly with the partner university regarding your application. All required documents will have to be uploaded on their platform or sent by email before the deadline (see the Americas Teams channel for each application deadline). If you have not received anything yet, it means your nomination has not been sent yet, please be patient.


In the past the partner has asked for the following:

  • Online application form
  • Photocopy of passport / Residence permit (valid more than 6 months after return)
  • Official English test certificate
  • Proof of financial resources form accompanied by a bank letter dated less than 6 months and the amount of which is a minimum of $21,000
  • A cover letter in English
  • (A copy of your visa if you have stayed in the United States in the 6 months preceding your application)

This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


To be given to Epitech bachelor campus administration to reenroll for the Tech4 (in April/May):

  • The addendum to the contract
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier


2. Visa (more information here)

You can find all the detailed information on the US government website or the Embassy of the US in Paris website.


1/Admission letter and I-20 form

When you have been admitted to UC Berkeley Extension, you will receive an I-20 form allowing you to apply for the F-1 student visa at the embassy. Please check the information on I-20 carefully and sign the document.


2/Pay the SEVIS fees

 You must then pay the SEVIS I-901 fees online (here). Make sure you print the receipts. The fees for students are $350.


3/Complete the DS-160 form

Complete DS-160 form and upload an ID photo meeting the following requirements. Print the application form confirmation page to bring to your interview.

You will have to pay a visa application fee (non refundable) before your interview of $185 (more information here).


4/Schedule an appointment at the consulate

For people in France, you need to make an appointment for your interview at the US Consulate. Plan to travel to Paris for it.

If you live in another country, check the different consulate/embassy.

You can check the deadlines for obtaining an appointment for submitting a file, here.


During your interview at the consulate, you must:

  • have the necessary supporting documents to prove that you qualify for the category of visa that you request--document relating to your current studies and its relationship to the studies you wish to pursue in the United States: academic transcript, various certificates, SAT or TOEFL test scores, diplomas, etc.
  • demonstrate, with supporting evidence, to the consular officer that you have solid family, social and financial ties to France and that you intend to return there once your residence permit has expired.
  • prove that you have the financial means necessary to finance your studies and live in good conditions in the United States for the first 12 months. Any document proving your family or relational ties with any person funding your studies, as well as bank statements, tax notices thereof.

Please note that the visa gives you the right to work 20 hours on campus.


3. Insurance and Health

It is imperative that you take out insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student. To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information.

For more information, you can consult the country’s health file at: https://www.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fr/conseils-aux-voyageurs/conseils-par-pays-destination/etats-unis/


Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.


4.Prepare your arrival

For advice to travelers issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs on the US, click here.

Check the International Student Checklist provided by the university here.

courses:
Credits

It is necessary to reach 24 units/local credits, i.e. 12 per semester, to have the 60 ECTS necessary to validate the year internationally.


Academic Calendar

Mid-August to mid-May


Department and Courses

The program will be taught in English and is not a diploma. It will focus on pre-selected business areas, such as entrepreneurship, leadership innovation / management, and new product development, and will include activity-based teaching.

You will find the details of the program here (Graduate Track):

https://extension.berkeley.edu/international/academic/bhgap/curriculum/#!#entrepreneurshipS22CG


Berkeley Haas Global Access Program (BHGAP) Curriculum

Graduate Track – Fall 2024 – Spring 2025


To earn the BHGAP Diploma Certificate (2 semester program), students must complete the following:

  • Students must enroll in at least 12 units and not more than 15 units per semester in all courses taken at the University of California
  • Students must complete a minimum of 9 units of BHGAP Curriculum (core and electives) each semester
  • Students will be automatically enrolled in BHGAP core courses
  • Students must complete at least 18 units of BHGAP curriculum over the duration of the program
  • Courses will not be counted twice for credit
  • Students must complete a minimum of 1 unit through the concurrent enrollment system each semester enrolled
  • Students must complete a minimum of 24 units of courses taken at the University of California


Additional requirements:

  • Students must successfully complete all courses with a grade of C or better
  • Students must earn a final program GPA of 2.5 or higher based on all courses taken
  • P/NP courses will not count toward final GPA. If a course has a standard grading option, students must select it during registration

Courses are subject to change. For questions, contact bhgap@berkeley.edu.



  • Required Core Course – Fall 2024

BUS ADM X419.7 Thriving at Haas and Beyond

1 Unit

This course includes coaching sessions, company site visits, and cohort talks. Topics range from personal development to career strategy, CSR, and leadership. Includes two essay assignments.


  • Innovation Core Courses – Fall 2024

(Must take at least one)


MBA XB290T Product Management – 3 Units – Vince Law

An introduction to product lifecycle, customer analysis, roadmap planning, stakeholder engagement, and team management.


UGBA XB39E-1 AI Ethics for Leaders – 2 Units – David Harris

Covers AI fundamentals, ethical frameworks, key ethical dilemmas, and organizational approaches to AI ethics.


MBA XB295 Entrepreneurship – 3 Units – Arman Zand & Ken Wilcox

Explores the startup journey from ideation through IPO, covering market strategy, team building, and financing.


MBA XB296 Data Science Applications in Finance – 2 Units – Donatella Taurasi

Applies analytics to finance and accounting, identifying problems and using tech solutions.


MBA XB290E Climate Change and Business Strategy – 3 Units – Andrew Isaacs

Covers 35 topics on how business interacts with climate change and how strategy influences climate outcomes.


  • Elective Courses – Fall 2024

UGBA XB196SB Innovation and Entrepreneurship for Sustainability – 3 Units – Darcelle Lahr

Explores the distinction between social and traditional innovation, with a focus on sustainability.


UGBA XB168 International Marketing – 3 Units – Wasim Azhar

Examines global marketing strategies, branding, pricing, distribution, and advertising across various world regions.


  • Required Core Course – Spring 2025

BUS ADM X419.7 Thriving at Haas and Beyond

1 Unit – Jennifer Davis

Repeat of Fall core course structure with updated site visits, coaching, and essay requirements.


  • Innovation Core Courses – Spring 2025

(Must take at least one)

MBA XB295 Entrepreneurship – 3 Units – Arman Zand

Continuation of the Fall course on launching and growing entrepreneurial ventures.


MBA XB296 Marketing Strategy in a World of Digital Disruption – 2 Units – Peter Wilton

Covers leadership, digital trends, and transformation strategies in business environments.


Equitable Design Lab – 2 Units – Mathieu Aguesse

Teaches an adaptive framework integrating co-design, systems thinking, and design thinking to create inclusive solutions.


Brands and Sustainability – 3 Units – Judy Hopelain

Examines the intersection of brand leadership and sustainability, with case studies and practical frameworks.


UGBA XB196SA Business Models for Sustainability – 3 Units – Andrew Isaacs

Focuses on how businesses adapt to climate change and create sustainable strategies and economies.


  • Spring 2025 Electives

EWMBA XB267 The Business of AI – 1 Unit – Matthew Stepka

Intro to AI with applications, trends, policy, legal implications, and business integration.


EWMBA XB252 Negotiation and Conflict Resolution – 3 Units – Holly Schroth

Covers negotiation theory and practice using simulations and case studies.


MBA XB269 Pricing – 3 Units – Wasim Azhar

Covers behavioral economics, innovative pricing models, and internet-based pricing strategies.


Important Notes

  • Presence in class is compulsory, under penalty of loss of visa and repatriation to France at the student's expense (impact on credits).
  • The courses are most likely more academic than at EPITECH.
  • The course list is given for information only. It can change from year to year.
  • If a course is not available when you arrive on site, EPITECH cannot be held responsible for it.
  • Any Tech 4 abroad involves an EIP! Take advantage of the free slots you will have to advance it.
cost:
Financial Overview (4th Year EPITECH)

  • You must pay the tuition fees for the 4th year of EPITECH, as well as the re-registration fees and related fees.
  • EPITECH covers the application fees and part of the tuition fees. Epitech covers tuition only for required credits.
  • The tuition supplement payable by you is indicated at the top of this page (if applicable).
  • Other costs at your expense include: travel, accommodation on site, insurance, and everyday expenses (books, food, transport, etc.).


Other Expenses / Estimated budget (more information here)


The local currency is the Dollar. 1 € = 1.16USD (rate as of October 2025).

Please check the Numbeo website to compare the cost of living between your city of origin and your city of exchange. Please note that everyone's budget will be different according to one's lifestyle.

For an apartment on campus, the budget will be higher.


The partner university estimates the total amount of your fees to be $21,000 for an academic year. You should budget at least $1,500 / month.


  • Round trip flights: around 1100€ for an AF direct flight
  • Application fee: $100 (non-refundable)
  • Student experience fee & equipment fee if you live on campus: 85$ and 110$
  • Health insurance : $900 cfor Fall/Spring, $510 for Summer (*Health insurance is included in the overall program fee unless otherwise stated)
  • Additional international insurance: 300-600€ depending on the company & coverage
  • Visa application fees: about 500€
  • Books $1000
  • Transportation: 800$
  • Miscellaneous and personal: 2800$
  • Housing and food (on campus): about 20 000$/year (see "accommodation" section)


These prices are indicative and may vary.
